I think the only problem I have with this show is how contradicting the MC seems to be. On one hand he seems disgruntled with having to work, yet he's so good at what he does. He led an attack on a dragon without hesitation, and so on. Just doesn't seem to mesh with the background of someone only doing the bare minimum to support his hobby. I was kind of expecting to see more of it here, as it feels like there was some form of character growth skipped here. I dunno, maybe it'll be addressed later, but that has bothered me.

That being said, I'm still enjoying it. The fight against the dragon was a nice bit of action, and it looks like next episode we're likely to learn more about the three foreign females that'll likely make up some form of harem. But will his friend ever find his CAT GIRL!? That's the real question here.

I think the source of that flipflop MC personality is that at its core, the show is very much wish fulfillment - an otaku with a respectable job who's also good at it! Problem is, being good at this job in particular requires a personality that is inherently incompatible with the "I don't give a shit" attitude. Sure, in the military, you can and do have some great guys who have a carefree personality, but the key there is that they still get the job done ("the unit jokester"). What you don't see is people who don't care, because that kind of attitude will either get you disciplined or outright discharged (attitude drives actions).

So therein lies the problem - the show wants an otaku protagonist, but in order to be the hero this wish fulfillment needs he can't act like an otaku which defeats the point.

I've got a respectable job, and I'm an otaku. I'm sure there are other otaku who have respectable jobs too. Honestly he's on of the few protags I'm even able to identify with anymore in regards to having a job.

The carefree attitude on the other hand is probably just a mechanism for relating confidence. Humans equate them together.

I kind of like it because it's a throwback to the Irresponsible Captain Taylor anime.

That all said, in a high stress job I find it believable that being carefree in the first place is a way to be effective. Lots of people freak out and make horrible decisions in combat because their brains blank or haywire. In WWII the trend was documented that until combat there was no way of telling if a soldier would actually be effective after just basic training, many soldiers would just pretend to participate in combat firing into nothing, or avoid combat altogether and flee.

Whether it's correct or not, those who are mentally able to find combat as trivial have always been troped as efficient fighters and leaders in combat, because normal people just plain have a really hard time dealing with it in the first place. Even normal people who have been trained reach their wits end and break in a lot of situations.

Literally bai' muajjal means a credit sale. Technically, it is a financing technique adopted by Islamic banks that takes the form of murabahah muajjal. It is a contract in which the bank earns a profit margin on the purchase price and allows the buyer to pay the price of the commodity at a future date in a lump sum or in installments

Yeah, it doesn't work that way. Nobody is going to give interest free loans, so Islamic banks charge a straight fee for a loan - it ends up amounting to the same thing, they just word it in such a way as to be considered technically halal.

The straight fee is also not allowed, actually. The way it works is that the bank doesn't actually ever loan you any money, instead they buy the house you wanted and lease it to you. Periodically you buy a share of the house, and then eventually you own 100% of it. You also have to pay rent while you're living there, though as you buy back the house the share owed to the bank goes down.

They don't actually get interest free loans. The way the arrangement actually works is that the bank outright buys the house, then rents it to you. When you pay rent, you also pay an additional fee to buy back a percentage of your home's equity. Over time, you eventually buy back 100% of the equity, at which point you own the home. Also, as you buy back the equity, the bank's share of the equity goes down (along with the amount of rent you owe the bank).

It's funny how we can write out so many different technicalities on paper that work out to the same actual events in the real world: the person lives in the house and pays the bank until he's paid the selling price of the house and then some, at which point he stops having to pay.

Usually when I post my updates I include my data as well. It looks like this: http://i.imgur.com/cz58YmK.png

I've had a few people ask me for a copy and I've always put off fully automating it so that you don't need to know how to use excel to make it work and to set it up for the first time. So I went ahead and did that. I know it's not perfect and there are some things that could be improved so please give me feedback if you use it.

The reason why I made this was because none of the weight trackers out there had all the information I wanted. These are the questions I wanted answered when I look at my weight loss chart:

  • I weigh 275 pounds and want to get to 198, how long will it take me if I lose 2 pounds per week average? Or 1.5 pounds, etc
  • How much have I lost so far?
  • How much am I losing per day?
  • How much am I losing per week?
  • Am I above or below where I should be right now?
  • If I keep losing at this pace, what date will I ACTUALLY hit my goal?
  • How many pounds until I hit my goal?
  • How long have I been on this weight loss journey?
  • How many more days until I hit my goal?

I wanted all of this information at a glance and pretty to look at. I know it's not an app or super fancy but if you're like me, like seeing this kind of data, and making the information visible helps you stay accountable, you'll like this too.

You'll need a Google account for this to work.

Click here to get a copy for yourself

I included a "HELP" tab in the spreadsheet but here's a run down of that help and information.

  1. To use this chart first you need a google account. Then click File, then MAKE A COPY. Name it whatever you want. Once you have your own copy, you can then fill out the green boxes on the right. Put in your Start date, Start Weight, Goal Weight and Goal Pounds per week (how much you want to lose per week).

  2. Hover over the chart to see floating summary box. If the floating box does not appear, click the chart, then click the eyeball icon in the upper left to enable "VIEW MODE". If you have any questions, message me or email likwidtek@gmail.com. Hope this chart helps you as much as it is helping me!

  3. Make sure to weigh in at least every Saturday. You can weigh in as much as you want but you will need those Sat totals if you're interested in what you're actually losing every week. If you don't have a chance to weigh in on saturday, just retype your most current weight into the box next to Saturday.

  4. Pick a goal that is reasonable. Don't expect that you're going to lose 4 pounds a week. Make sure your goal is POSSIBLE. If you don't know, ask your doctor or chose something like 1 pound a week. Additionally this dynamic spreadsheet will only work up to 1,000 rows. If your number of days is larger than 1,000 rows, email me at likwidtek@gmail.com and I will make you a custom sheet.

Many Thanks to waz_here for her help on one of the bigger formulas, TuxedoJacob for his awesome idea on how to automate some of it and a huge thanks to my wife for keeping me motivated and on track in my own weight loss.
